article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Fire OG Kush × Afghan Haze
Breeder: Gage Green Genetics
THC Content: 23%
CBD Content: Up to 3%
Terpene Profile: limonene , caryophyllene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Lemon, cedar, pine, fuel, hash, herbs, pepper
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Inferno Haze was created to bring two very different sides of American cannabis together without allowing either one to disappear. Gage Green Genetics paired the clone-only Fire OG Kush, famous for dense resinous flowers and penetrating fuel, with a vigorous Afghan Haze male carrying longer growth, cerebral intensity, and old-school Haze character. Released as the first strain in Gage Green’s Private Collection, the resulting F1 became notable for its range of expressions: some plants lean toward compact OG-style buds, while others reveal longer Haze calyxes and more pronounced stretch.

The most celebrated selection, known as the Uno phenotype, combined exceptional potency with a distinctive woody-citrus aroma and enough CBD to make its cannabinoid profile unusual for a high-THC cultivar. An original laboratory report circulated by Gage Green showed that selection at 23.616% THC, while later breeder material commonly listed it near 23% THC and 3% CBD. Beyond the numbers, Inferno Haze is defined by contrast: lemon and cedar against fuel and hash, cerebral acceleration followed by physical calm, and Haze flower structure reinforced by the density of Fire OG.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-confirmed cross is Fire OG Kush × Afghan Haze. Contemporary documentation from the original release identifies the mother specifically as a clone-only Fire OG Kush selection and the father as a vigorous Afghan Haze. Fire OG represents the California side of the pedigree, drawing from the broader OG Kush family and contributing dense flowers, heavy resin, fuel, lemon, pine, and a powerful physical component. Rather than using an easier commercial Haze hybrid as the other parent, Gage Green chose Afghan Haze, giving the cross a deeper combination of Afghan body and traditional Haze cerebral traits.

The pairing produced an F1 population rather than a narrowly uniform clone line, so phenotype variation is part of the authentic Inferno Haze experience. Gage Green’s original description emphasized that different expressions could appear, while its preferred plants produced very large, dense buds, sweet aromatics, and uplifting effects. That variability later became useful breeding material in its own right. Inferno Haze went on to appear in Gage Green projects and other hybrids, and an F2 generation was eventually produced to expose an even broader range of OG- and Haze-dominant characteristics.
Effects and Experience

Inferno Haze tends to announce itself quickly. The first stage can produce a pronounced head rush, with mental energy rising sharply before the body has fully responded. Attention may become more expansive, conversation livelier, and music or visual stimulation noticeably more immersive. The Afghan Haze parent is particularly apparent during this period, contributing a cerebral character that can feel uplifting and thought-provoking rather than immediately sleepy. Gage Green’s original description specifically highlighted an uplifting mental effect in favored phenotypes.

Time changes the direction of the high. Fire OG begins to anchor the experience with progressively stronger physical relaxation, turning the initial rush into a longer and more settled state. The mind may remain active while muscular tension eases, although larger amounts can eventually produce considerable heaviness and mental haze. This progression makes the cultivar more versatile than a purely stimulating Haze but more mentally active than a conventional heavy OG during its opening phase.

Potency can be substantial. The famous Uno selection tested above 23% THC in an archived laboratory report, and breeder material also recorded approximately 3% CBD in that particular plant. Those values should not be treated as universal specifications for every seed-grown Inferno Haze plant. As an F1 hybrid, cannabinoid production can vary noticeably among phenotypes, and cultivation, harvest maturity, curing, and laboratory methodology further influence measured potency.
Medical Benefits

The combination of rapid cerebral effects and sustained physical relaxation has made Inferno Haze especially interesting to consumers who use medical marijuana but do not necessarily want immediate sedation. Some may prefer a smaller amount when seeking temporary mood elevation or relief from everyday stress, while the later physical phase may be useful when bodily tension or discomfort is also present. The comparatively high CBD measurement reported in the Uno phenotype is particularly unusual, although consumers should never assume that every plant carrying the name contains 3% CBD.

Gage Green historically described the selected Inferno Haze cut as one of its particularly potent medicinal plants, and the Uno phenotype later became breeding material in additional projects. That reputation is not equivalent to clinical evidence. Inferno Haze has not been proven in controlled trials to treat pain, anxiety, insomnia, depression, nausea, or any other medical disorder. THC-rich weed can also provoke anxiety, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, or impaired coordination in sensitive consumers. Anyone using cannabis medicinally should rely on the laboratory analysis of the actual product rather than expecting the cannabinoid profile of a famous historical phenotype.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Inferno Haze develops one of those aromatic profiles in which the two parents remain easy to imagine. Cedar and dry wood provide a distinctive foundation, while lemon, pine, fuel, pepper, and resinous hash fill in the edges. Historical material describing the Uno selection specifically points to a woody citrus aroma and pine-hash flavor. Other expressions can move toward sweeter fruit or candy aromas, reflecting the greater variability expected from the original F1 population.

Grinding the flower usually intensifies the sharper side of the profile. Lemon peel and pine can become more noticeable before diesel-like OG pungency and spicy herbs emerge underneath. On the inhale, citrus and wood may lead; the exhale tends to reveal more fuel, pepper, earth, and hash. Some phenotypes produce longer Haze-style calyxes that accompany a darker incense-like fragrance, while OG-dominant plants may smell substantially more gassy and resinous.

No standardized terpene profile was published for the original seed population. Limonene would fit the lemon and citrus side, pinene the evergreen qualities, caryophyllene the peppery spice, and myrcene the earthy resinous depth. Those associations are useful for understanding the aroma but should not be presented as a fixed chemical formula without batch-specific laboratory testing.
Growing Information

Inferno Haze combines Haze vigor with much denser flower formation than growers might expect from the name. The original seed release was suitable for indoor, outdoor, and greenhouse cultivation, with approximately 60 days of flowering commonly associated with the strain. That relatively quick finish is notable considering the Afghan Haze parent. The Haze side can still produce noticeable vertical stretch, so indoor gardeners should leave adequate space before initiating flowering.

Plant structure varies with phenotype. OG-leaning individuals can form broad, dense flowers with substantial calyx stacking, while Haze-oriented plants may produce longer spear-like buds or foxtailed structures. Gage Green’s preferred original phenotype was selected in part because it combined large, dense flowers with potency and a sweet aroma. Topping or low-stress training can be useful for more vigorous individuals, particularly when several branches are competing for the top of the canopy.

Because the original release was an F1, growers searching through a seed population should expect selection to matter. One plant may remain more compact and fuel-heavy while another stretches farther and emphasizes cedar, citrus, or Haze traits. That diversity became part of the strain’s breeding value and eventually led Gage Green to explore the line further through Inferno Haze F2.

Indoor yields are best described as medium to high rather than assigned an unsupported universal figure. The breeder highlighted large, dense flowers but did not establish a dependable grams-per-square-meter specification for the original release. Outdoor cultivation favors warmth, abundant sunlight, and enough autumn weather to finish around October. Dense OG-influenced flower structures also make airflow and humidity control important as harvest approaches.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Inferno Haze?
Inferno Haze is Fire OG Kush × Afghan Haze. Gage Green Genetics created the original F1 using a clone-only Fire OG Kush mother and a vigorous Afghan Haze father.
Who bred Inferno Haze?
Inferno Haze was created by Gage Green Genetics, also known as Gage Green Group. It was released as the first cultivar in the breeder’s Private Collection series.
How much THC does Inferno Haze have?

Potency varies by phenotype, but the celebrated Uno phenotype tested at approximately 23% THC. An archived 2012 reference to Gage Green’s original laboratory report gives the more precise result of 23.616% THC.
What does Inferno Haze taste like?
The strain commonly combines cedar, lemon, pine, fuel, herbs, pepper, and hash. Certain phenotypes can become noticeably sweeter, while OG-dominant plants tend to emphasize fuel and resin.
How long does Inferno Haze take to flower?

Approximately 60 days is the commonly documented flowering time for the original Gage Green cultivar, putting most plants near the eight-to-nine-week range. Individual phenotypes can finish somewhat earlier or later.
Final Thoughts on Inferno Haze

Inferno Haze demonstrates why combining OG and Haze genetics became such an influential direction in American cannabis breeding. Fire OG supplies resin, density, fuel, pine, and physical strength, while Afghan Haze introduces stretch, cedar, cerebral intensity, and greater aromatic range. Instead of forcing those qualities into a perfectly uniform plant, Gage Green’s original F1 preserved enough variation for growers to find markedly different expressions.

The Uno phenotype became the standout, with laboratory testing above 23% THC and an unusually notable CBD level reported around 3%. More broadly, this cannabis strain offers dense resinous flowers, approximately two months of flowering, and a progression from forceful cerebral stimulation into sustained physical calm. Its cedar-lemon-pine-hash profile also distinguishes it from the fruit and dessert hybrids that dominate many modern marijuana menus.

For enthusiasts exploring Gage Green Genetics history, Inferno Haze is particularly significant because it was more than another Fire OG cross. As the first entry in the breeder’s Private Collection and a parent subsequently used in additional genetic projects, it became a foundation for later work while retaining an identity of its own: vigorous Haze growth, OG flower density, strong cannabinoid potential, and one of the more distinctive woody-citrus profiles in the Gage Green catalog.
